messages.subject: Using DSM some newbie troubles
parts:
Hello everyone,

I've been exploring the dsm and Distance packages on R and I'd like to know if:
-there's any way one can apply the size bias regression method to the ds R code?
-in a dataframe of 5 years of observation data, can I obtain a dsm model per year using the same global(5year) detection function?

Best regards,

Jorge

messages.author: 9b03386432b784c0
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Using DSM some newbie troubles
parts:
Olá Jorge, list ;)

(sorry folks for the "patriotic" wording above, but It's good to get Portuguese questions in this forum, not that often it happens!)

Regarding the questions:

- To the best of my knowledge in these R packages cluster size has to be included in the analysis as a covariate, no option for using size bias regression.

- implementation details apart, but I'm assuming this is possible in dsm, you can use a pooled detection function across years to predict density on a year by year basis in a DSM. However, you have to ask yourself the following: does it make sense that you do not have enough detections to estimate a detection function per year, which typically has a small number of parameters associated with, but then you have enough data to estimate a density surface model each year, which probably requires more parameters to specify any way? I guess you could fit a common model across years (so really a spatio-temporal model) which includes variables which change each year, hence borrowing strength across years using a pooled model that then is used to make predictions per year, but I'm not sure that is possible off the shelf in dsm (and my first guess would be no...) so that might not be something you want to get into to begin with.

I hope this helps, others feel free to add

cheers

T

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Using DSM some newbie troubles
parts:
Hi Jorge, hi listfolk,

Just to follow-up on Tiago's answers...

- The current set of R packages don't have any functions to perform the
size-bias regression (though it is, of course, possible to code this up
in R) -- using a covariate in the detection function seems like a better
option though.

- Certainly the setup you describe of a single detection function used
in yearly DSMs should work, though one should be careful setting up the
observation data frame to ensure that only the correct detections are
included (dsm may complain about this, if it does drop me an e-mail).
I'll echo Tiago's comments, that building a separate model per year
discards the possible information between years, even if you have lots
of data. That being said, building a fully spatiotemporal model in dsm
is still experimental -- in the sense that we don't have good advice on
what form the model should take in particular situations (and there are
many possible modelling options). See e.g. this thread:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/distance-sampling/fvjVYQIn4kw/9FwzGsWcCQAJ

Hope this helps!

best,
--dave
